summary.headline: Catalogue of Prohibited Astrological Books
summary.text: Apomasar’s account and commentary on a catalogue of prohibited apotelesmatic books kept in the Constantinopolitan imperial palace, discussing its Byzantine or Arabic provenance and dating it between Isaac ben Salomon and the 1388 Codex Angelicanus. The listed works include those of Stephanus of Alexandria, Aristotle, and Theophilus son of Thomas, with references to Hermes, Valens, and Palchus.
